title: tunnel: don't remove a secret after a failed inspect
body:
The remote `SecretRm()` inspects every secret before removing it, but only handles a 404 from the server. Any other error response falls through to the removal path with a nil inspect report:

```go
secret, err := secrets.Inspect(ic.ClientCtx, name, nil)
if err != nil {
	...
	if errModel.ResponseCode == 404 {
		...
		continue
	}
}
allRm = append(allRm, &entities.SecretRmReport{
	Err: secrets.Remove(ic.ClientCtx, name),
	ID:  secret.ID,
})
```

So podman-remote calls `Remove()` for a secret it failed to inspect and then crashes on `secret.ID`. The server returns 500 for any lookup error other than "no such secret", and the easiest one to get is an ambiguous ID prefix. With 20 secrets, three of which have IDs starting with `4`:

```
$ podman --remote secret rm 4
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
[signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x8 pc=0x12bee22]

goroutine 1 [running]:
go.podman.io/podman/v6/pkg/domain/infra/tunnel.(*ContainerEngine).SecretRm(...)
	pkg/domain/infra/tunnel/secrets.go:92 +0x4c4
go.podman.io/podman/v6/cmd/podman/secrets.rm(...)
	cmd/podman/secrets/rm.go:40 +0x7c
...
```

(note: this trace is trimmed)

The local `podman secret rm 4` reports `secret is ambiguous` for the same setup.

With this change the remote client puts the error into the report for that name, the same way the local implementation reports per-secret errors, and doesn't try to remove it:

```
$ podman --remote secret rm 4
Error: inspecting secret 4: more than one result secret with prefix 4: secret is ambiguous
```

Removing by name, `--ignore` and a mix of existing and missing names behave as before.

The new e2e test creates 17 secrets, so at least two IDs share the first hex character, and checks that removing by that prefix fails cleanly and leaves all secrets in place.

Found by Linux Verification Center (linuxtesting.org) with SVACE.
